we have designed a model of hard real-time multiprocessor systems that allows us to analyze their feasibility in a WCET-free manner.
we have developed a model and an algorithm to analyze the operational feasibility of hard real-time multiprocessor systems with exact CPU loads.

we have designed a model for the operational behaviors of systems compatible with their time specifications, that this model can be used for feasibility decision of hard real-time multiprocessor systems, and that the feasibility of a system is independent of the exact values of its task WCETs.

we have shown that the feasibility decision problem for systems with exact CPU loads is NP-Complete.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed a method for analyzing the operational feasibility of hard real-time multiprocessor systems, and that this method is based on regular language theory.
we have developed a method that allows the designer to validate the feasibility of the system without any knowledge about the actual WCET values.
the feasibility decision problem is decidable for the model we have introduced, and we have also obtained an algorithm to compute a solution to the problem.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed model is a powerful tool for aiding designers to check the consistency between the system and its time requirements.
